description: Who is behind the curtain? Find out with describing words, watch the Zoo Sign Machine change animals, and learn plurals with -s, -es and -ies.

youtube.title: Describing Words Zoo! Adjectives and Plurals for Kids | Grade 2 Grammar | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Pink, curly, muddy... who is behind the curtain? Robo and Cat guess zoo animals from describing words (adjectives).
The Zoo Sign Machine makes Bear big (and tiny, oops!), Bunny sleepy and Pig wiggly. Then learn plurals: ducks, boxes, bunnies, toys, and the sheep surprise.
Play at home: hide a toy and give three describing words.

do.text: Describing Words Zoo
Our new zoo friend is behind this curtain.
I'll give you clues, one describing word at a time.
Clue one: pink.
Clue two: curly.
Clue three: muddy. Who is it?
Pink, curly and muddy? I think it's a pig.
Oink! Hello! Look at my curly tail.
You found her with just three describing words!
Muddy is my favourite describing word!
Thank you, Pig! Let's meet another friend.
The duck.
the duck
Now listen. The yellow, splashy duck!
But why do we need describing words? A duck is a duck.
Describing words tell us what something is like.
They paint a picture in your head.
Another name for a describing word is an adjective.
adjective
A describing word tells about a naming word, like duck.
Okay, so splashy tells me how the duck plays. I like that.
Describing words often come before the naming word.
Describing words can tell six kinds of things.
Colour! The yellow duck swims.
colour
Yellow tells the colour. I can see it in my head.
Size! The big bear yawns.
size
Is this bear big or small? Shout it out!
Big! Big is a size word.
Shape! The round ball rolls.
shape
Round tells the shape. A round ball rolls, a box doesn't.
Feel! The fluffy sheep naps.
feel
Fluffy tells how the sheep would feel if you touched it.
Sound! The noisy dog barks.
sound
Number! Three chicks peep.
number
Number words are describing words too? Huh. Nice.
Remember Pig? Muddy was a describing word too.
Fun fact: pigs roll in mud to keep cool.
Pigs can't sweat much, so the mud cools them down.
Clever pig. Muddy, and cool.
Now meet my Zoo Sign Machine!
When I change the word, the animal changes to match!
Big!
The big bear. Stretch up tall like the bear!
big
Hmm, let's try another size word. Tiny!
Robo! Bears aren't tiny!
Oops! You're right. Big bear!
And here's the same idea another way. The bear is big!
Curl up small like a tiny bear. Now stretch up big!
Here comes Bunny. Sleepy!
Shh. The sleepy bunny. Now... awake!
Wiggly! Wiggle with Pig!
A yellow duck. And now... two ducks!
Colour words work too. Here's a red ball.
Purple!
Okay, that machine is pretty cool.
Two ducks. When there's more than one, we say plural.
plural
Plural means more than one. Listen to the end of the word.
One duck, two...?
Ducks! Most words just add s.
The s is the clue that there's more than one.
Chick, chicks. Frog, frogs. Cat, cats!
But listen to this one. Box.
One box, two...?
Boxes! Box, e s.
But why add e s? Why not just s?
Try saying box-s. It's hard! Your tongue gets stuck.
So we add a little extra beat. Box-es. Boxes!
Words ending in s, x, s h or c h add e s.
-es
Bus, buses. Dish, dishes. Bench, benches.
Clap the extra beat with me. Bench-es. Dish-es!
Some words end in y. Watch what happens to bunny.
One bunny, two bunnies! The y leaves...
and i e s comes in! Bunnies!
Puppy, puppies. Berry, berries.
Wait. Toy ends in y, and we say toys. Why?
Great catch! Before the y in toy, there's a vowel, o.
Vowel and y? Just add s. Toy, toys. Key, keys.
Now here's a surprise. One sheep...
Two...?
Two sheep! Sheep stays the same.
Fun fact: a group of sheep is called a flock!
flock
Fish is like that too. One fish, two fish.
One y word, two y words. Can you spot the y leaving?
So most words add s, and a few stay the same.
Clap along! Tell me more!
Tell me more, tell me more, what's it like? Tell me more!
Is it big? Is it small? Is it yellow, round or tall?
Tell me more, tell me more, what's it like? Tell me more!
Fluffy, noisy, one or three, describing words for me!
Tell me more, tell me more, what's it like? Tell me more!
Challenge time! The curtain is back.
A new friend is hiding. Here are three clues.
Brown.
Furry.
Big. Who is it?
It's Bear! Brown, furry and big.
Three clues were enough. Brown, furry, big. I knew it.
Bonus clue! There are five of them.
They are small, yellow and fluffy. Who are they?
Five chicks!
Play it at home! Hide a toy and give three describing words.
I'll go first. Round, red, bouncy.
A ball! Then swap and let your grown-up give clues.
Quiz time! Find the describing word.
The fluffy sheep naps.
Fluffy! Fluffy tells us what the sheep is like.
Question two. One fox, two...?
Foxes! Fox ends in x, so we add e s.
Question three. One puppy, two...?
Puppies! The y changes to i e s.
Last one. Why do describing words help?
They tell us what something is like, so we can picture it.
Zoo closing time! Goodbye, friends!
Now that's a well-described zoo.
Today we used describing words and plural endings.
Tell me more next time! Bye!
